sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Graves County, KY?
sections.html:
Record it at the Graves County Clerk's office in Mayfield. Kentucky ties the filing to the land: a deed must be recorded in the county where the property sits, or where the greater part of it sits, to be effective against later buyers without notice and against creditors.

The Clerk's office is at 1102 Paris Road, Suite 5, Mayfield, KY 42066, with listed hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The county's page names the office as the place where deeds, mortgages and other encumbrances are recorded and kept for public use. Calls about real estate records go to the records vault at (270) 247-1697. The general line, which also covers title transfers and marriage licenses, is (270) 247-1676.

The same office also collects delinquent real estate tax, so a seller with an old balance can clear it and file the deed in one visit.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record in Graves County?
sections.html:
The fees are set by KRS 64.012, and the 2026 version took effect on July 15, 2026. A deed of up to five pages costs $33 to record and index. A mortgage of up to 30 pages costs $63. Both add $3 for each page beyond the limit, and the clerk may also take a $10 reimbursement for permanent storage of the record.

Selected Graves County Clerk fees under KRS 64.012 (source: Kentucky Revised Statutes, effective July 15, 2026)
ServiceFee
Record and index a deed (up to 5 pages)$33.00
Each extra page on a deed$3.00
Each added reference to the same instrument$4.00
Record a mortgage (up to 30 pages)$63.00
Deed of release of a mortgage or lien$33.00
Acknowledging or notarizing a deed$5.00
Certified copy of a record$5.00, plus $0.50 a page after three

Of the $33 deed fee, $6 goes to the state's affordable housing trust fund and the clerk keeps $27. The transfer tax comes on top of these amounts.

sections.h2: What must a Kentucky deed contain before the Clerk will take it?
sections.html:
The Clerk is barred from filing a deed that skips the contents required by KRS 382.135, so errors are caught at the counter. A deed to real property has to carry the following.

  • The full names and mailing addresses of the grantor and the grantee.
  • A statement of the full consideration paid.
  • An in-care-of address where the property tax bill for the year of transfer may be sent.
  • A sworn, notarized certificate, signed by both sides, that the stated consideration is the full price. For a gift, the certificate says so and gives the estimated fair cash value.

KRS 382.110 adds a source-of-title rule. The deed has to name the immediate source of the grantor's title, with the book, page and recording date of the prior deed. If the owner got the land by inheritance, the deed must say how and from whom.

Deeds that convey only utility easements, cemetery lots, rights-of-way for government agencies, or corrections of earlier deeds are excused from the consideration statement, tax-address and sworn certificate items.

sections.h2: How does an inherited Graves County house reach the buyer?
sections.html:
When a house passes by will or intestate succession, the personal representative of the estate has to file an affidavit with the county clerk of each county where the property lies before closing out the estate. It lists who receives each property and the value used in handling the estate, or says no value was set.

That affidavit sits alongside the deed. A Graves County heir selling to a cash buyer should therefore expect two filings at the Clerk's office, the affidavit and the new deed, with the deed charged under the schedule above.

The deed also has to carry the acknowledgment required by KRS 382.270. Under that statute, a deed or mortgage is not valid against a buyer for value without notice, or against creditors, until it has been acknowledged or proved according to law.

sections.h2: Who pays the transfer tax on a Graves County sale?
sections.html:
The seller does. KRS 142.050 puts the tax on the grantor named in the deed, at fifty cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500, and the Clerk will not accept the deed until the tax is paid. For a sale at the Census median of $147,800, that is 296 units of $500, so the tax would be $148.

The Clerk keeps 5 percent of what it collects and sends the rest to the county treasurer every three months. Transfers made only to secure or release a debt, between spouses in a divorce, or under a foreclosure are excused, as are nominal-value transfers between parent and child or grandparent and grandchild.

Anyone recording a survey or subdivision plat pays a separate $40 per page for maps up to 24 by 36 inches, so a seller splitting off acreage should budget for that too.

sections.h2: How are mortgage releases and assignments handled?
sections.html:
A paid-off mortgage is cleared by a release recorded at the Clerk's office. KRS 382.360 allows a margin entry or a separate deed of release, and it makes plain that handing a release to the borrower does not replace filing it with the Clerk. A seller whose lender never filed a release can find the old mortgage still open on the record at closing.

When a lender sells a mortgage to another holder, the new holder must file the assignment with the Clerk within 30 days. Failure to record an assignment does not by itself affect the validity of the lien.

Before listing, ask the records vault to confirm that every earlier mortgage on the parcel shows as released. An open mortgage that was actually paid is easier to fix before a buyer's title search finds it.

sections.h2: What is Graves County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Graves County lies in far western Kentucky, in the Jackson Purchase, and covers 552 square miles of land. It was formed in 1824, and its seat is Mayfield. The county is also home to Wingo and part of the Clarks River National Wildlife Refuge. Dark-fired tobacco farming and clothing manufacturing both figure in its history.

The December 10, 2021 tornado caused major damage in Mayfield, including to the courthouse. Census QuickFacts gives these figures for the county:

  • Population: 37,050 in 2025, with 14,139 households.
  • Owner-occupied homes: 76.1 percent, with a median value of $147,800.
  • Median gross rent: $775, and mean travel time to work of 20.7 minutes.
  • Retail sales of $808,990,000 in 2022, about $22,168 per resident.

A seller who keeps the recorded paperwork in order, from the last deed to the mortgage release, avoids the delays that title problems cause.

faqs.q: Which office records deeds in Graves County, KY?
faqs.a: The Graves County Clerk, at 1102 Paris Road, Suite 5, Mayfield. The records vault line is (270) 247-1697, and the listed hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: How much does the Graves County Clerk charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: $33 for a deed of up to five pages under KRS 64.012, plus $3 per extra page and a $10 storage reimbursement. The transfer tax is collected separately at recording.

faqs.q: Can the Clerk refuse my deed?
faqs.a: Yes. KRS 382.135 bars the Clerk from filing a deed missing the required names, addresses, consideration statement, tax-bill address or sworn certificate. A deed also must name its source of title.

faqs.q: Do I need to record a mortgage release before selling?
faqs.a: Yes, if the lender has not already done so. Giving the release to the borrower does not replace filing it with the Clerk, so ask the records vault whether it shows on the parcel.

faqs.q: What does an estate file with the Graves County Clerk before an inherited house is sold?
faqs.a: The personal representative files an affidavit naming who receives each property and its estimated value. KRS 382.135 requires it before the estate is closed out, in each county where property lies.
